text:
The trade from Toronto made Matthew Knies the face of a deal, and the first month in Columbus has been hard. Through 15 games he has 2 goals and 7 points, after 23 goals and 66 points for the Maple Leafs last season, and the coverage has noticed (one Yahoo Sports headline: "Maple Leafs’ Trade of Matthew Knies Takes Brutal New Turn").

Our numbers say this isn't mostly bad luck. Over his last ten games he has 3 points and no goals, against about 7.3 we'd expect at his ice time, and his own chances have dried up: 1.7 expected goals on his shots, against 2.6 usual. Expected goals measure how dangerous the chances were, so that's a real dip, not just hot goaltending.

The tools haven't gone anywhere. He's still playing more than 18 minutes a night, his top shot speed ranks in the 83rd percentile, and our talent range for him centers on 2.38 points per 60, well above the 1.54 he's producing now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 56% of his shots coming off the rush last season. We'd watch whether Columbus can get him playing in transition more; that's where he does his damage.
headline: Matthew Knies and a slow start in Columbus
